title: POC weekly sync - quantization INT8/FP8
summary: Weekly POC sync to review INT8 vs FP8 quantization runs. INT8 gives ~1.5-1.8x throughput and ~30-40% memory savings with small quality regressions on long-tail prompts; FP8 gives a middle ground with better quality but smaller perf gains. Agreed next steps: run full-suite A/B eval on 2k token seqs, reproduce perf on dedicated instance, and share detailed quantization report and configs.

transcript:
Header: 2026-05-05 14:00 PT | Duration: 45m
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nambiar (Redwood SE), Jared Kim (Acuity ML), Sasha Lee (Acuity Infra), Marta Ruiz (Acuity DS)

Summary: quick recap of last week's runs; went deeper into FP8 artifacts; looked at a couple of outliers; agreed on next steps.

Links referenced: quant-report-v2 (drive link), benchmark-spreadsheet: https://redwood.app/benchmarks/acuity-quant-v2 (note: placeholder)

Topics: perf numbers, quality deltas, config tweaks, deployment plan.

00:00 Alex: Okay everyone, thanks for joining, we'll keep it to 45 minutes. Quick roll call, then Priya will walk through the INT8/FP8 runs.
00:12 Priya: Hi all, thanks. So high level: INT8 runs reduced model size by roughly 45% on disk and gave about 1.6x throughput on our baseline T4-ish equivalent, FP8 was more conservative — size down ~25% and throughput ~1.25x but quality looked closer to FP32.
00:35 Jared: Wait, when you say throughput is 1.6x, that's tokens/s end-to-end or just inference kernel? I want to be sure we're comparing apples.
00:44 Priya: Good call — these numbers are end-to-end tokens/sec measured with our net pipeline and batching enabled (batch size 8 baseline). p50 latency dropped from ~180ms to ~120ms for typical 512-token requests, p99 improved from ~600ms to ~420ms on INT8. FP8 p50 was around 140ms, p99 ~480ms.
01:10 Sasha: Are those runs on the hosted infra or on dedicated instances? We saw different behaviour last week when we ran on our in-house nodes.
01:18 Priya: These were on Redwood's dedicated test cluster (equivalent cards), not your exact infra. We recommended repro on your dedicated instance.
01:25 Marta: Any sign of increased hallucination or factuality drop with INT8? That's our main worry — throughput is great but we can't accept a measurable regression on the NER/extraction tasks.
01:40 Priya: On the standard prompt set (2k examples) we saw a ~0.6% drop in exact-match for the extraction eval, and logprob deltas were small: avg logprob decreased by ~0.12. For most intents the differences are marginal, but the long-tail factual prompts had higher variance — some examples failed where FP32/FP8 were fine.
02:05 Alex: To set expectations: INT8 tends to move the needle on memory and throughput but you'll need to vet it on your critical prompts. FP8 looks like a good compromise if you need higher fidelity.
02:18 Jared: Can we get a breakdown by sequence length? Our workload has a fat tail — we push up to 2k tokens regularly.
02:26 Priya: Great question — current runs concentrated on 512 tokens. We did spot checks at 1024 with similar relative gains, but we haven't fully profiled 2k. That's on the action list.
02:40 Sasha: Also curious about KV cache behavior — we saw increased cache misses previously and some unexpected memory growth. Did you enable contiguous KV caches in the runtime?
02:50 Priya: We did, but there were a couple of experiments where the memory allocator and quantization interplay produced higher transient RSS on sequence growth. We'll include allocator flags and recommended GC/eviction settings in the report.
03:05 Marta: Any weird tokenization differences? Sometimes token-level distributions change under quantized weights and that affects scoring.
03:12 Priya: Not at tokenization level, more the downstream probability mass shifts for rarer tokens. We'll surface a few examples in the report (we noted the exact prompts).
03:30 Speaker 1 (possible transcription mislabel): so the net impact is — INT8 is high perf, small quality hit; FP8 is mid perf mid quality.
03:40 Alex: Yep. We also tested batching sensitivity: INT8 benefits more from larger batch sizes up to ~12-16; beyond that p99 latency climbs. For lower latency you can run batch size 1 with smaller perf gains.
04:00 Jared: How about quantization-aware calibration? Did you run per-channel or per-tensor calibration?
04:08 Priya: We ran per-channel symmetric quant for weights and dynamic quant for activations, using the calibration set you shared. Per-channel gave us better accuracy retention. We'll include the calibration script.
04:28 Sasha: Is there an easy fallback strategy? E.g., run INT8 normally but for anything flagged low-confidence route to FP8/FP32?
04:36 Alex: Exactly, that's a recommended pattern — threshold on logprob or a cheap heuristic to fallback. Redwood's routing can do per-request routing to a higher-quality variant when needed.
04:50 Marta: Any major pitfalls we should look out for when flipping a canary to INT8?
04:56 Priya: Watch for those long-tail prompts, metrics divergence on your eval set, and memory transient spikes during long-context requests. Also pin CUDA/cuDNN/kernels to the versions we tested — kernel selection matters.
05:15 Jared: On the perf numbers: can you put the raw CSV in the sheet so we can slice by seq len / batch / concurrency?
05:22 Priya: Yep, will upload the raw CSV and a condensed summary.
05:28 Alex: Next steps recap: Redwood sends the quantization report + config snippets; Acuity runs A/B on 2k seqs and schedules the dedicated-instance perf repro. We'll sync mid-next-week.
05:40 Jared: Sounds good. Also please include a short note about cost impacts — model runs per token cost delta for INT8 vs FP8, ballpark.
05:48 Alex: We'll include a pricing delta slide and a decision matrix.

-- Questions / Notes --
Q: How big is the quality regression in real terms? A: Small on aggregate but present on edge cases, need to validate on your prompt set.
Q: Can we do mixed-mode? A: Yes — use INT8 for bulk traffic, FP8 for SLA-critical endpoints or high-fidelity routes.

Final recap (last 2 minutes):
Alex: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the report (Priya) and you'll run the 2k test (Jared). Next call: 2026-05-12, same time.

Crosstalk/notes: occasional overlaps, speaker labels sometimes generic (Speaker 1/2), some words mis-transcribed ("K-V cash" for KV cache, "F-P eight" for FP8).
